title: Multiply 3-digit numbers by 1-digit numbers (area model, partial products)

lesson.title: Big Numbers, Small Steps: 253 Times 3

steps.say: You already know how to break a number apart to multiply, like two tens and five ones. Today we do the same trick with a three-digit number, so a big multiplication turns into three easy little ones.

Imagine three crates of BC apples, and each crate holds two hundred fifty-three apples. We draw a rectangle three rows tall and two hundred fifty-three wide, then slice it by place value into two hundred, fifty, and three.

visual.caption: One big rectangle sliced into three friendly pieces

steps.say: Now multiply each piece by three. Two hundred times three is six hundred. Fifty times three is one hundred fifty. Three times three is nine. Those three answers are called the partial products.

visual.caption: Three partial products, three pieces of the rectangle

steps.say: Last step: add all three pieces back together. Six hundred plus one hundred fifty is seven hundred fifty, and seven hundred fifty plus nine is seven hundred fifty-nine apples.

Here is the mistake I see most often. Some kids multiply the hundreds and the ones, get six hundred plus nine, and write six hundred nine. But they forgot the middle slice, fifty times three. That whole one hundred fifty piece of the rectangle just disappeared! So always count your slices: three slices means three partial products before you add.

visual.caption: The missing middle slice is worth 150

steps.say: So remember: split the big number by place value, multiply every piece, then add them all back up.

lesson.answer: Split by place value, multiply every piece, then add them all back — never leave a piece out.

practice.question: A bakery in Victoria fills four big boxes of muffins, and each box holds one hundred thirty-two muffins. Draw your own area model: split one hundred thirty-two into one hundred, thirty and two, multiply each part by four, then add the three partial products. How many muffins altogether?
practice.answer: One hundred times four is four hundred, thirty times four is one hundred twenty, and two times four is eight. Four hundred plus one hundred twenty plus eight is 528 muffins.
